name_structures.description: Every Congolese is designated by a name of one or more elements; the prénom, the nom and the postnom are the elements of the name (art. 56). Names are drawn from Congolese cultural heritage (art. 58); the child bears the name chosen by the parents (art. 59)
name_structures.source: DRC, Code de la famille (consolidated 2017), arts 56, 58, 59 (https://www.leganet.be/Legislation/Code%20de%20la%20famille/CDF.2017.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

name_structures.description: Members of one family who share a nom must each add different complementary elements (art. 57); a parent who passes on their name must add at least one element different from their own (art. 61). So relatives may share one element, never the whole name
name_structures.source: Code de la famille (2017), arts 57 and 61, read 5 Nov 2026

name_structures.description: A married woman keeps her name; during the marriage she may add her husband's name to hers, and a widow who has not remarried may keep using it (art. 62)
name_structures.source: Code de la famille (2017), art. 62, read 5 Nov 2026

name_structures.description: Authenticité: from 1971-72 Christian (European) given names were banned and replaced by ancestral names; nom + postnom became the identity. From 24 Apr 1990 Christian names could again be used in daily life but not in registers or official documents; from 1997 they could be registered again. Adults born before about 1997 may have records without the prénom they use
name_structures.source: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Réponse aux demandes d'information (doc 449451), citing Ndaywel è Nziem (1998), 'De l'authenticité à la libération : se prénommer en République démocratique du Congo', Politique Africaine; Pauwels & Pintens (1983), 'La législation zaïroise relative au nom' (https://www.droitcongolais.info/files/Hum.Sc.-NS-_T.XLVII,2_PAUWELS-J.-M.et-PINTENS-W._La-legislation-zairoise-relative-au-nom.-Droit-et-authenticite-africaine_1983.pdf); read 5 Nov 2026

name_structures.description: Modern Congolese names combine locally rooted Bantu elements with Christian or French-origin elements
name_structures.source: Tshabu Ngandu et al. (2026), 'CongoNames Corpus', Data 11(7):169, abstract via the corpus repository (https://github.com/bernard-ng/drc-names-corpus), read 5 Nov 2026

order_rules.description: The order in which the name elements were declared, and their spelling, are immutable (art. 56); changing a name, its spelling or its order needs a court (art. 64)
order_rules.source: Code de la famille (2017), arts 56 and 64, read 5 Nov 2026

order_rules.description: Since 1990 the prénom may precede nom and postnom, but written identity long continued to ignore prénoms while speech used them. A record may hold nom + postnom only, and an oral report the prénom only
order_rules.source: Ndaywel è Nziem (1998), p. 104, quoted by IRB Canada (doc 449451)

order_rules.description: Forms with first/last fields (UNHCR, other countries) do not follow the declared order: the postnom is dropped, or nom and postnom are swapped (Mutombo Kalala Pierre / Pierre Mutombo)
order_rules.source: SCOPE.md §1 (DRC); BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3; ICC, Annex 1, 'The issue of names used to identify citizens of the DRC' (SCOPE.md [S9])

phonetic_rules.description: Lingala has seven vowels (e/ɛ, o/ɔ distinct); the 1976 standard writes ɛ and ɔ, but everyday writing uses e and o, and tone is almost never marked. Search forms fold ɛ to e and ɔ to o; the original form is kept
phonetic_rules.source: Wikipedia, Lingala, 'Writing system' (Société Zaïroise des Linguistes, 1976), accessed 5 Nov 2026; APiCS Online, survey chapter 60, Lingala

phonetic_rules.description: Lingala has no uniformly accepted spelling; the same writer varies. Semivowel y is written i, y or not at all; w as w, o, u or not at all; close-mid o as o or u; a word-initial prenasal written or not (sango / nsango)
phonetic_rules.source: APiCS Online, survey chapter 60, Lingala (https://apics-online.info/surveys/60); Wikipedia, Lingala

phonetic_rules.description: Congo Swahili is written with the standard Swahili alphabet: ch, sh, ny, ng' as single sounds; prenasalised mb, nd, nj, ng, mv, nz. Its regional varieties (Kivu, Katanga, Maniema, Ituri) differ mainly in grammar; spelling differences in names are not documented
phonetic_rules.source: Wikipedia, Congo Swahili and Swahili language, accessed 5 Nov 2026; Bose (2016), 'Morphosyntactic core features of Kivu Swahili', Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online

phonetic_rules.description: Names from eastern DRC show r/l alternation in attested aliases, as well as nasal insertion and loss (patterns from the UN 1533 sanctions list aliases)
phonetic_rules.source: UN Security Council Consolidated List, 1533 (DRC) entries, aliases (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B12]); used for patterns only, no names copied

common_administrative_forms.description: Nom + postnom as the identity on documents issued 1972-1997, without a prénom

spelling_conventions.source: Wikipedia, French orthography (RESEARCH_LOG.md [P3]); Wikipedia, Lingala (French-influenced ou for [u] in the Republic of the Congo)

spelling_conventions.note: Chichewa (Malawi) writes its single r/l sound by the preceding vowel; a Malawian clerk may apply it to a refugee's name. Swahili itself keeps r and l apart
spelling_conventions.source: Wikipedia, Chewa language (1973 orthography); Lyons & Mchombo, Chichewa Grammar; Wiktionary, Chichewa entry guidelines

relationship_implications.note: The law requires relatives who share a nom to differ in another element, and a parent who passes a name to add one. Sharing one element is evidence of a possible link; sharing all elements suggests the same person, not relatives. Different noms are common among siblings and are no evidence against kinship
relationship_implications.source: Code de la famille (2017), arts 57 and 61; SCOPE.md [S5]

known_failure_modes.description: Adults registered 1972-1997 may have no prénom on documents while using a Christian prénom in daily life; a search by prénom misses the record and a search by nom + postnom misses the oral report
The postnom is dropped, or taken as a surname, in forms with first/last fields
A married woman's name may carry her husband's name added after hers; compare with and without it
Lingala spelling varies by writer and within one writer (glides, o/u, initial nasal, French spellings)
The Christian prénom changes form with the writer's language (Jean / John / Yohana / Jeannot); handled by the cross-pack given-name data (week 4)
Places renamed after 1971 and in the 2015 provincial reform (old and new province names coexist in records)
A legal name change by court (art. 64) or by adoption (art. 63) is a change, not a variant; it is never a public edge
known_failure_modes.source: Code de la famille (2017), arts 63-64; NAME_CHANGE.md rule 1

protected_or_sensitive_forms.description: The pack holds no ethnic, clan, tribal or religious marker, and names are never used to infer one; this matters in eastern DRC, where names have been read as markers of group membership
protected_or_sensitive_forms.source: SCOPE.md §4; THREAT_MODEL.md T8, T18; DATA_RULES.md DR-1.7

protected_or_sensitive_forms.description: Names adopted in exile are not variants; tracing across a name change uses the protected-person route
